{{Quote|The Bpfasshi don't like Jedi. They had some trouble with Dark Jedi during the Clone Wars, and chased them as far as Dagobah.|Leia Organa Solo, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Heir to the Empire 2">[[Heir to the Empire 2|''Heir to the Empire'' 2]]</ref>}}
The '''Bpfassh Uprising''' was a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] insurrection that wreaked havoc in the [[Sluis sector/Legends|Sluis sector]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], while the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] were beginning. It started when a group of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Bpfassh]] fell to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] due to the pressure of the war. To oppose them, the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] formed a task force led by [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] himself. Thanks to his intervention, the insurrection was quelled, marking one of the first major victories of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in the third year of the Clone Wars. The Dark Jedi from Bpfassh, however, had not spoken their last word.

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Clone Wars concluded, and the despotic [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was formed. Shortly afterwards, the Bpfasshi Dark Jedi resumed their attacks in the Sluis sector, engaging in a large space battle. At the end of that battle, the last of the Dark Jedi seized the ship of the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Jorj Car'das]] ship and took it to [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]]. Ironically, that planet was the new residence of Yoda, who was hiding from the Jedi-hating Empire. Once again, the Bpfasshi darksider was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by the Grand Master.

Despite Yoda's victory, the Bpfassh Uprising was best remembered as a fiasco. Many years after the events, the Bpfasshi still had a deep-seated resentment against the Jedi, and the incident was still discussed in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|With the transmission of Articles of Secession to the Senate, Senator Corlissi Ludar made formal the withdrawal of the Sluis sector from the Republic.|HoloNet News Report|<ref name="HNN49">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|news/13328_4.html|Sluis Sector Secedes; Seswenna Restates Loyalty}}</ref>}}
[[File:Planet26-Bpfassh-SWR.png|thumb|left|The crisis originated on Bpfassh, in the Sluiss sector.]]
In the last [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Bpfassh]] in the [[Sluis sector/Legends|Sluis sector]] hosted an [[Bpfassh enclave|enclave]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. However, that [[Jedi chapter house/Legends|chapter house]] had a long history of rebelliousness to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|High Council]], the governing body of the Order.<ref name="TNEC" /> In the third [[Standard month/Legends|month]] of the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] 13 post-[[Great ReSynchronization]], the Sluis sector officially seceded from the Republic to join the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="HNN49" /> A few months later, the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] broke out between the Republic and the separatist Confederacy. Due to their superior combat experience, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were led to play a pivotal part in the conflict, becoming the [[General/Legends|generals]] and [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] of the new [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|army]] of the Republic.<ref name="TNEC" /> However, there were Jedi who doubted the war and refused to receive their martial promotion from the High Council. Those dissidents formed an informal movement<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu">''[[Jedi: Mace Windu]]''</ref> that was also joined by those who invoked the [[Right of Denial]], a tradition that allowed Jedi to protest against a decision made by the High Council.<ref name="Marching Orders">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/lf20050727marchingorders|text=Marching Orders|int=Marching Orders}}</ref> The whole Jedi academy of Bpfassh ended up joining the movement too.<ref name="TNEC" />

==The uprising==
===Initial insurrection===
[[File:Nejaa_Halcyon.jpg|thumb|Nejaa Halcyon was instrumental in the destruction of the Bpfasshi Jedi.]]
{{Quote|It wasn't just Bpfassh, either—some of those Dark Jedi escaped and made trouble all throughout the Sluis sector. One of them even got as far as Dagobah before he was caught.|Leia Organa Solo, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="HttE" />}}
As the Clone Wars went on, the Sluis sector went trough continual fighting. Because of its affiliation with the Confederacy of Independent Systems, the sector was being pressured by the Republic forces based on [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], in the neighboring [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]]. Additionally, the [[Sons and Daughters of Freedom]], a crew of Republic [[Privateer/Legends|privateers]] led by [[Zozridor Slayke]], kept raiding the sector. Ultimately, that situation provoked a spike of martial zealotry among the Jedi of the Bpfassh academy. Although they had initially refused to get involved in the ongoing conflict, the Bpfasshi Jedi gave in to their anger and fell to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. They set themselves against Slayke's men and were responsible for a rampage of terror and destruction throughout the Sluis sector. Eventually, the High Council sent a task force of loyal Jedi to quell the Bpfassh uprising. [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], the [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the Jedi Order himself, was part of that force.<ref name="TNEC" /> At one point, Yoda was pitted against at least three adversaries armed with [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]].<ref name="JVS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> The [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Ylenic It'kla]] was also part of the Jedi task force, and so was [[Nejaa Halcyon]],<ref name="FF28" /> a [[Corellian Jedi]] who had already [[Battle of Praesitlyn|fought]] in the Sluis sector<ref name="JT" /> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> The latter in particular was instrumental in putting down the uprising,<ref name="FF86" /> although he was slain in the fighting,<ref name="I Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref><ref name="Lone Wolf">{{StoryCite|story=Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke|book=SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story}}</ref> and the details of his involvement would be lost in the mists of time.<ref name="FF28" /> Eventually, Grand Master Yoda [[Lightsaber/Legends|dueled]] the leader of the Dark Jedi and defeated him.<ref name="TNEC" />

===Post-Clone Wars resumption===
{{Quote|They'd been operating for about fifteen years when he was accidentally caught up in the middle of a big battle between some Bpfasshi Dark Jedi and—well, basically everyone else in that sector. According to Car'das's later story, one of the Dark Jedi commandeered his private ship and forced them to take off.|Talon Karrde|<ref name="VOTF" />}}
[[File:Yoda_Dagobah.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Grand Master Yoda had taken refuge on Dagobah.]]
A few months later, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of the Galactic Republic, who was secretly a [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] named [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious, revealed his true colors to the galaxy. As the Clone Wars were brought to an end, the Republic was [[Declaration of a New Order|replaced]] by a tyrannical Galactic Empire led by Sidious himself. As the Empire sought to [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|exterminate]] all Jedi, Yoda, the former victor of the Bpfassh Uprising, retreated to a self-imposed [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] on Dagobah,<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> a swamp planet of the Sluis sector.<ref name="db">{{DB|location|dagobah|Dagobah}}</ref> At that time,<ref name="SAV" /> however, the sector in question experienced a resurgence of Bpfasshi Dark Jedi activity,<ref name="VOTF" /> despite Yoda's earlier victory over their leader. At some point, a large space battle erupted between the darksiders and the combined forces of everyone else in the sector. A [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] named [[Jorj Car'das]], who ran the former business of one [[Booster Terrik]],<ref name="FF86" /> was accidentally caught up in the middle of the fray. As the space battle drew to a close at the darksiders' expense, one of the most powerful of the Dark Jedi captured Car'das' vessel, forcing the smuggler and his four crewmen to take off. He immediately killed one of Car'das' men by tearing his body apart, and turning the other three into mind-controlled puppets. However, the Dark Jedi left the smuggler captain himself mostly alone, presumably as the darksider needed Car'das' knowledge of ports and hyperlanes to make his escape.<ref name="VOTF" />

The Dark Jedi demanded passage to Dagobah,<ref name="VOTF" /> either seeking sanctuary or Yoda's hiding place. As soon as Car'das put down his ship at the edge of Dagobah clearing, Yoda himself made an appearance, as if he had been expecting a dark visitor. The resulting battle between the two Force-users lasted nearly one day and a half, during which, according to Car'das, "the swamp blazed with fire and lightning." Eventually, Yoda got the upper hand. The Dark Jedi perished, disintegrating in a [[Dark side burst|burst of energy]]. Car'das and what was left of his men had also taken part in the fighting, but only the smuggler had survived. Yoda then healed the wounded man and sent him on his way.<ref name="VOTF" /> The death of the Bpfasshi Dark Jedi left a lasting stain on Dagbobah, which further helped Yoda to hide himself from the Imperials.<ref name="FF86" />

==Aftermath==
[[File:Jorj.jpg|thumb|Jorj Car'das, last witness of the Bpfasshi Uprising's endgame.]]
{{Quote|We were still getting echoes of the whole fiasco in the Imperial Senate when I was serving there.|Leia Organa Solo, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="HttE" />}}
Following the chaos of the Clone Wars and the rise of Palpatine's Empire, many historical records were either destroyed or tampered with. [[Historian/Legends|Historians]] still knew that the Jedi task force had succeeded in their mission and that the last Dark Jedi had made his or her way to Dagobah, but they surmised that the darksider had been destroyed either by the natural hazards of the swamp planet or by Halcyon and his men.<ref name="FF28" /> Additionally, the Bpfassh Uprising was conflated with<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|90|Bpfassh}} treated [[Jorus C'baoth]]'s involvement with the [[Bpfasshi/Legends|Bpfasshi]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] as a legend. {{CSWECite|I|161|Dagobah}} positively identified [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] as the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who stopped the [[darksider]]s.</ref> that of a [[Dark Jedi uprising|similar event]] that had involved Master [[Jorus C'baoth]].<ref name="RPGRCR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook]]''</ref> Indeed, when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], the first of a [[New Jedi Order|new generation]] of Jedi, searched the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate's]] records on Jorus C'baoth<ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref> in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]],<ref name="TERC" /> he read that C'baoth had fought the Dark Jedi on Bpfassh,<ref name="Dark Force Rising" /> while he had in fact defeated darksiders in the [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]] at some point before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]].<ref name="RPGRCR" /> However, Jorj Car'das was still alive, and could testify on Yoda's decisive involvement. In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], he told his story to two individuals&mdash;[[Talon Karrde]] and [[Shada D'ukal]].<ref name="VOTF" />

Although the Bpfassh Uprising had been efficiently brought to an end, the inhabitants of Bpfassh remained wary of all Jedi. Many years later, echoes of the incident were still heard in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]],<ref name="HttE" /> the ruling council of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="ROTS" /> In 9 ABY,<ref name="TERC" /> nearly three decades after the events, the former Imperial [[Senator/Legends|senator]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] still remembered what she had heard about the Bpfasshi fiasco during her years of service.<ref name="HttE" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Origin===
{{Quote|One of the more subtle goofs in Heir is in the dating. At the time, George hadn't settled on the final time line, and we were told that the Clone Wars took place thirty-five years before ''A New Hope''.|Timothy Zahn|<ref name="HE20">''[[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition]]''</ref>}}
The Bpfasshi insurrection was first mentioned in ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'', a [[1991]] novel and the first entry in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s so-called [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|''Thrawn Trilogy'']]. In the novel, Luke Skywalker is advised to stay away from Bpfassh, as some of that its Jedi "went bad" during the Clone Wars, leading to resentment toward their order. Skywalker also learns that the cave in which he confronted a [[Dark Spirit|vision]] of his father was first tainted with dark energies years before, when Yoda killed a powerful Bpfasshi Dark Jedi on Dagobah during the Clone Wars. According to Princess Leia, that duel must have occurred thirty to thirty-five years before the novel's present time,<ref name="HttE" /> which would put it between [[26 BBY/Legends|26]] and [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].<ref name="SimpleMath">Those dates are derived using simple math based on the fact that, according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', the events of [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|''The Thrawn Trilogy'']] occurred in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]].</ref> In ''[[Dark Force Rising]]'', the second entry in the ''Thrawn Trilogy'', it was mentioned that Jorus C'baoth was part of a taskforce assembled to oppose a Dark Jedi insurrection on Bpfassh.<ref name="Dark Force Rising" /> In [[1997]] and [[1998]], Zahn published ''[[Star Wars: The Hand of Thrawn Duology]]''. In the series' second and final tome, titled ''[[Vision of the Future]]'', the smuggler Jorj Car'das tells the story of how he was kidnapped by a Dark Jedi who took him to Dagobah, where the darksider got beaten by Yoda. According to Car'das, those events took place 45 years before the novel's present time,<ref name="VOTF" /> which would still be 26 BBY.<ref name="SimpleMath2">Those dates are derived using simple math based on the fact that, according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', the events of ''[[Star Wars: The Hand of Thrawn Duology]]'' occurred in [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]].</ref>

===Retcons===
With the release of the [[prequel trilogy]] between [[1999]] and [[2005]], the course of ancient events invented by Zahn for his trilogy was compromised. Initially, the Clone Wars were supposed to have taken place thirty-five years before [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], but the prequels showed they only started in 22 BBY and ended in 19 BBY. Because of that, all the dates featured in the ''Thrawn Trilogy'' are off by sixteen years.<ref name="HE20" />

In ''The Official Star Wars Fact File'', a 140-issue magazine published from [[2002]] to [[2005]], two conflicting account of the Bpfasshi Uprising's endgame were given. According to the 28th issue, the death of the Dark Jedi leader was thought to have been caused by either the natural hazards of Dagobah or a Jedi task force led by Nejaa Halcyon and Ylenic It'kla.<ref name="FF28" /> Despite that, the 86th issue of the ''Fact File'' confirmed Yoda's responsibilities in the darksider's demise.&mdash;while also mentioning Halcyon's participation in the mission.<ref name="FF86" /> However, the ''Official Fact File'' were meant to be the real-life equivalent of a [[New Republic Centralized Archives|centralized database]] created by the New Republic in 27 ABY, which implies it may contain inaccuracies from an in-universe point of view.<ref name="SWFF1">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 1|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 1]]</ref> Incidentally, the 28th issue does state that many historical records were either altered or lost following Palpatine's rise to Emperor, and presents its information as surmises.<ref name="FF28" />

Morever, the script of the 2005 movie [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] specified that Yoda had never been on Dagobah before his exile at the end of the Clone Wars.<ref name="SWI98">{{InsiderCite|98|Star Wars Q&A|''Star Wars'' Q&A}}</ref> The reference book ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', which was released a few months after the movie, included a retelling of the Bpfassh insurrection. While omitting the problematic endgame on Dagobah, that new account established a connection between the uprising and the Jedi dissident movement<ref name="TNEC" /> that appeared in other sources such as ''[[Jedi: Mace Windu]]''.<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" />

In [[2008]], the canonicity of the Bpfasshi uprising was brought up in the [[Star Wars Insider 98|98th issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine. [[Lucasfilm]] official [[Leland Chee]] stated that Yoda's battle against a Bpfasshi Dark Jedi as described in Zahn's novel was no longer part of continuity. However, Chee said that "a mortally wounded darksider made it to Dagobah after a confrontation with Yoda, but the battle did not take place there."<ref name="SWI98" /> The problem was solved a few months later, when the roleplaying game sourcebook [[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']] retconned the incident with Car'das, the Dark Jedi and Yoda to have happened ''after'' the Clone Wars.<ref name="SAV" /> Since they do not contradict each other, the present article considers that Yoda fought Bpfasshi Dark Jedi both during and after the Clone Wars.
